- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward spikes in price; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment is low and price is trending upward, model underreacts — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to capture momentum.
- Model shows persistent lag in capturing short-term reversals; if sentiment shifts sharply downward after a peak, reduce forecast by 1–3% immediately.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate mean-reversion zones — if recent 10-day average is higher than 30-day average, forecast should be slightly below that average.
- If sentiment is high and price is flat or declining, model overreacts — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid overcorrection.
